title: もらう and てもらう: the receiving verb
summary: もらう is a pull-verb: you receive something or an action, and the giver takes に. It behaves like the receptive, not like くれる.

blocks.text: もらう is usually grouped with あげる and くれる, but the grouping hides how it really works. **あげる** gives up; **くれる** gives down to me or my group. Both are tied to a particular giver and receiver. **もらう** is also "downloading", but it is a **pull** where you take the initiative, and it works much more like the receptive れる / られる (lesson 13).
With a noun, もらう need not name any giver at all: 一万円をもらった, "(I) got ten thousand yen". If you do name the giver, mark them with **に** (or から).

After the て-form, もらう means "get someone to do it for me". The carriage is the receiver, and the person who does the action takes に, exactly like the doer in a receptive sentence. The difference is in the feeling: **られる** says something simply happened to you, **てもらう** says you brought it about.

rows: The teacher praised me. (it happened to me)
I got the teacher to look at it. (I asked)

blocks.text: Many English renderings are misleading. お医者さんに見てもらう is not "see a doctor" but "have a doctor look at me". 散髪をしてもらう is "have my hair cut" with nobody named. Without a named doer, none is implied.
The receiver need not be you
くれる only suits you or your group. もらう has no such restriction. You can say about another person that they received something or got something done.

blocks.jp: 弟は兄に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
blocks.en: My younger brother got his older brother to help with his homework.

blocks.jp: 髪を切ってもらったほうがいいよ。
blocks.en: You should get your hair cut.

items: **もらう** = receive (a pull); the giver or doer takes **に**.
**Nをもらう** need not mention a giver; **Vてもらう** = get someone to do it.
It is closest to the receptive but adds "I brought it about".
Unlike くれる, the receiver may be a third person.

questions.instruction: Which particle marks the person who gives or does the action with もらう?
questions.note: Like the doer in a receptive sentence.

questions.prompt: 母に服を買ってもらった。
options: I got my mother to buy me clothes
I bought clothes for my mother
My mother bought clothes for herself
questions.note: 買って + もらった: received the buying.

questions.prompt: もらう always names the giver.
questions.note: 一万円をもらった names no giver.

questions.instruction: Which one stresses that the speaker took the initiative?
questions.note: もらう says "I arranged for it".

questions.instruction: Which sentence matches "have my hair cut"?
questions.note: 切って + もらう: get someone to cut it.

questions.instruction: Tap the person who did the helping
questions.note: に marks the doer in a もらう sentence.

questions.instruction: Why is もらう compared to the receptive?
options: Both describe receiving an action from someone
questions.note: In both the carriage is the receiver and the doer takes に.

options: 姉は先生に作文を直してもらった。
姉は先生を作文を直してもらった。
姉は先生が作文を直してもらった。
姉は先生で作文を直してもらった。
questions.note: The doer 先生 takes に.

questions.prompt: Unlike くれる, もらう can be used about someone other than the speaker.
(I) got my friend to check my essay.
questions.note: Doer with に, the thing, then the て-form + もらった.

questions.instruction: Which one is a push, where the giver acts first?
options: 友達が手伝ってくれた。
友達に手伝ってもらった。
questions.note: くれる is a push; もらう is a pull.

questions.instruction: Why is "see a doctor" a poor translation of お医者さんに見てもらう?
options: It really means have a doctor look at me
It means look at a doctor
It means to become a doctor
questions.note: The doctor does the looking; I am the receiver.
